row.evidence: gates-windows run 30682495436 vs gates-linux run 30682495455, same commit
row.statement: The Windows formal-gate failure is very likely a platform problem, not 19 model failures. Evidence is the asymmetry between runners on the same commit: gates-windows failed formal in about 37 seconds with run=19 matched=0 skipped=17 failures=19, while gates-linux spent over 9 minutes inside the same gate step still running. Zero matched rows plus near-instant completion is the signature of expectation rows never binding - a path or platform resolution issue in formal/run-checks.sh - whereas the Linux runner is doing real simulation work. Diagnose the matcher before treating any of the 19 as a genuine failure.

The formal suite behaves three different ways on the same commit, and only one of them is correct. On this WSL host it completes in 28 seconds with run=19 matched=19 skipped=17 failures=0, SUITE PASSED. On windows-latest it completed in about 37 seconds with run=19 matched=0 failures=19 - zero rows bound, which is a matcher or path fault, not 19 model failures. On ubuntu-latest the same gate step has run past 14 minutes without finishing, across three separate runs. Local timing rules out the suite being inherently slow, so the Linux CI behaviour is a hang or an environment stall and must be diagnosed from the completed log once the 60-minute job timeout fires.

row.evidence: /tmp/w1a-r6.log, lane-run v029-r6 first lines
row.statement: The WSL clock preflight cannot read the host clock and degrades to a warning, so it never actually compares drift. The host value is EMPTY, not skewed, so the refusal is not a drift finding at all - the check cannot obtain one of its two inputs and reports that as if it were drift. A preflight that cannot read a clock should say so distinctly from one that measured drift.

row.evidence: merge-base worker-cmd.sh agy branch vs adapters/agy.sh at lane/plan4-t1
row.statement: A load-bearing TRAP comment was lost when the agy branch moved into an adapter, and the architects T1 verification could not see it. worker-cmd.sh carried: TRAP: --print takes the PROMPT as its value, so it MUST stay LAST. Any flag placed after it is consumed as the prompt text and the lane fails silently. Do not reorder these for tidiness. It also carried the reasoning that agy encodes effort IN the model name, so no --effort is passed, verified against agy models on 2026-07-30. adapters/agy.sh keeps the correct argv ORDER but none of the explanation, and a grep of the whole tree finds neither. The constraint now looks arbitrary and is exactly the kind a later tidy-up removes. T1 was verified by counting functions and capability keys; comment preservation was never checked.

row.evidence: /tmp/audit-t2-verdict.txt, one line, no verdict block, 2026-08-01
row.statement: An audit lane can return narration and no verdict, and the absence of findings can be misread as approval. The grok audit of the T2 refactor emitted one line - Auditing the refactor diff... Checking the full adapter and shim files to verify byte-equivalence - and stopped. No VERDICT, no FINDINGS. The cause is the same single-burst limit that governs implement lanes: the prompt supplied only the DIFF, grok decided it needed the full files to judge equivalence, and the burst ended on that intent. An audit prompt must inline everything the auditor needs to reach a verdict, exactly as an implement spec must; and an audit result with no verdict line must be treated as a FAILED audit, never as a silent pass.

row.evidence: merge-base vs HEAD of skills/foreman/scripts/lane-run.sh readiness block, lane/vendor-iso
row.statement: Checking a suspected regression against the pre-change file prevented a false accusation. The reworked readiness gate appeared to introduce a fail-open, because enforcement is wrapped in a test that the probe exists. The merge-base version has the same shape. The new form enforces in a strict superset of cases - override set OR real probe present - so it is not weaker. The fail-open is genuine but pre-existing, and reporting it as introduced by this change would have been wrong.

The CI suite count is not stable run to run, which blocks criterion 2 independently of any defect. Five consecutive gates-linux runs on ascending commits: 12, 12, 12, 13, 11 failures against 537 tests. The 13 came from the traps-17 merge, which appended markdown to AGENT_TRAPS.md and nothing else - a docs-only change cannot break a test unless a structural or docs check reads that file, so this is either flake or a doc-structure assertion. The 11 is the gate-fixture merge landing, which removed exactly the two decision-events failures as predicted. Criterion 2 asks for three CONSECUTIVE green runs; with a count that moves by one on a docs-only commit, that is unreachable until the mover is identified.
row.supersede_reason: the first version could not distinguish flake from a docs-structure assertion; the per-slice diff names foreman-setup.bats as the mover and shows it self-healing on the next run

row.evidence: foreman-test-slices.tsv from runs 30683976294, 30684042600, 30684181710
row.statement: The CI suite count is unstable because tests/foreman-setup.bats is FLAKY, and that single test blocks criterion 2. Per-slice diff across three consecutive gates-linux runs: 30683976294 had 12 failures across 6 slices; 30684042600 had 13 across 7, the extra one being tests/foreman-setup.bats gaining a single failure on a commit that appended markdown to AGENT_TRAPS.md and changed nothing else; 30684181710 dropped to 11 as tests/decision-events.bats lost exactly its 2 failures, confirming the stale-fixture fix. foreman-setup failed once and passed again with no relevant change between, so it is flake rather than a docs-structure assertion. Criterion 2 requires three CONSECUTIVE green runs and cannot be met while it flaps.

row.evidence: local bats tests/foreman-setup.bats x3 = 4/4; foreman-test-slices.tsv columns; gates-linux job log
row.statement: The foreman-setup flake is CI-only and currently undiagnosable from CI evidence. Three consecutive local runs give 4 of 4, so the host reproduces nothing. The four tests are all grok readiness cases, and this repo already records that the readiness probe is network-flaky and couples unit tests to live vendor state - the same coupling just fixed for vendor-isolation via FOREMAN_TOOL_CHECK, which foreman-setup does not yet use. Naming the failing case is blocked by a harness gap: the uploaded artifact carries per-slice COUNTS, not per-test names, and the job log prints only the summary line. A suite that cannot say WHICH test failed on the runner cannot support a three-consecutive-green criterion.

row.evidence: six-run local replication of tests/foreman-setup.bats test 2, 2026-08-01
row.statement: NULL RESULT on the foreman-setup flake hypothesis. The idempotence test asserts byte-equality of two foreman-setup runs after stripping only lines starting with time:, which is the classic shape of a flake caused by a second time-varying field. Tested directly: six consecutive runs with the same grok shim produced ZERO differing pairs, and no ms/elapsed/duration/pid/tmp-looking field survives the strip. So the idempotence assertion is NOT demonstrably the flake, at least on this host. The cause remains unnamed and needs the CI per-test log (obligation 40) rather than another guess. Recorded because a plausible untested story is how a wrong fix gets shipped.

row.evidence: codex audit of lane/tap-log e0343ba; grep for GATE-line consumers across tests, .github, tools and skills returns only an unrelated gate-eval.sh string
row.statement: An audit BLOCKED because the architect gave the auditor acceptance criteria that contradicted the spec given to the implementer. The TAP-log spec explicitly instructed appending the log path to the GATE PASS and FAIL lines, following the pattern of the existing report path. The audit criteria said the change adds an artifact and nothing else. codex correctly flagged the output-line change as out of scope. The code is not defective: branching, return status and RESULT/TOTAL/REPORT extraction are untouched, and a grep shows NOTHING parses ci-local.sh GATE lines, so no consumer can break. The defect was in the instructions. When writing an audit prompt, derive its criteria FROM the implementation spec rather than restating them from memory.

Two decisions made this session now interact: the session store is tracked in git, and the new gates carry no path filter, so every checkpoint commit of .foreman/session.db triggers a full gates-linux and gates-windows run. Three runs were already queued within seven minutes. Decide which property to keep. A paths-ignore for .foreman/** is defensible - the store is data, not code - but it weakens the gates-everything property criterion 3 exists to establish. Do not silently add the filter; it is the owners call.

gates-linux duplicates formal.yml and is slow because of it. ci-local.sh includes the formal gate, and gates-linux calls ci-local.sh with no path filter, so every push to main now runs the full Quint commit tier - over 9 minutes and still running on the first attempt, against about 20 seconds for the other six gates combined. formal.yml already runs that suite on formal/** changes. Decide: drop formal from the hosted gates and leave it to formal.yml, or drop formal.yml and let the gates own it. Running both on every push is waste, and a 10-minute gate discourages the per-commit gating criterion 3 is meant to establish.

The Use-path readiness gate fails OPEN when no probe is available, and this predates the FOREMAN_TOOL_CHECK work. Both before and after, lane-run.sh only enforces LANE_READY when a probe exists: originally guarded on env/tool-check.sh being present, now on the override being set OR that file being present - a strict superset, so the refactor did not weaken it. But in a checkout where env/tool-check.sh is missing and no override is set, a lane spawns with NO readiness check at all and nothing says so. Decide: refuse when no probe can be found (fail closed), or emit a loud NOT-VERIFIED marker. Silently skipping a gate is the failure mode this release keeps finding.

The T2 argv-equivalence test freezes the pre-refactor builder as an IN-TEST COPY (legacy_implement_argv in tests/adapters.bats), not as a call into historical code. The architect verified the copy is faithful to the merge-base builder, and the grok audit approved it while flagging the standing risk: it is sound only while the copy stays independent of the adapters. If a future change edits both the adapters and that helper together, the test becomes circular and asserts nothing. Either add a comment forbidding edits to legacy_implement_argv, or replace it with a check that reads the builder out of git history at the pinned commit.

Identify why the CI bats failure count moved from 12 to 13 on the traps-17 merge, which changed only AGENT_TRAPS.md. tests/foreman-setup.bats is flaky on CI: one failure appeared on run 30684042600 and was gone on the next run with no relevant change between. The CI test artifact cannot name a failing test. tests/run.sh uploads foreman-test-slices.tsv with per-slice pass/fail/skip counts, and the job log carries only the GATE bats summary, so a CI-only failure like the foreman-setup flake cannot be attributed to a case. Capture per-test TAP output as an artifact - or at minimum the not-ok lines - so a runner-only failure is diagnosable without guessing. This blocks obligation 39 and, through it, criterion 2.
